(1) the IGF-IGF-IR axis may play a role in human breast cancer development and (2) IGF-IR could be a prognostic factor in breast cancer.
(1) the IGF-1R expression in primary breast cancer is associated with ERalpha status and (2) the expression of Bax protein is associated with lymph node status, tumor stage and grade of malignancy.
IGF-1 receptor is a negative prognostic marker in human breast cancer and its expression negatively correlates with estrogen receptor alpha.

the role of the IGF-I signaling pathway in breast cancer.
a new aspect of IGF-IR function in breast cancer and its relationship with ERalpha, Bax and Bcl- 2 proteins.
the IGF- IR, ERalpha and apoptosis associated proteins, Bcl - 2 and Bax in human primary breast cancers, and their relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IGF-1R expression is not associated with the clinical and pathological features of breast cancer and does not correlate with ERalpha, Bax and Bcl-1 expression.
IGF-1R and ERalpha are inversely correlated in the breast cancer and that the expression of Bcl-2 is positively associated with ERalpha expression.
the IGF-1R is a negative regulator of estrogen receptor alpha in breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IGF-1R expression was associated with ERα expression, and that ERα expression was associated with Bcl- 2 expression.

IGF-1R expression is not correlated with the expression of ERalpha in human breast cancer and that the negative correlation between the IGF-1 receptor and ERalpha expression is not associated with the lymph node involvement.
IGF-1R is an important factor in the progression of breast cancer and its expression may be an important prognostic factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of the IGF-I receptor in breast cancer tissue is not associated with the expression of estrogen receptors and Bax, Bcl- 2 proteins, which is in line with the literature data.
IGF-1R expression in breast cancer is associated with ERalpha status.
the expression of the IGF-I receptor in breast cancer may be a marker of poor prognosis and a possible therapeutic target.
